name: Out-of-bounds Write
principle: The program writes before the beginning or past the end of the intended buffer. This corrupts adjacent memory and can crash the process or overwrite control data for code execution.
detection_signals: strcpy, strcat, sprintf, gets, scanf("%s") writing into fixed-size char buffer
memcpy, memmove, strncpy, read, recv size argument not bounded by destination capacity
array[index] = value where index comes from input, parsing, pointer subtraction, or arithmetic without index < length check
loop writes buf[i] with condition i <= len or i <= sizeof(buf)
malloc/calloc/new allocation size omits terminator, sentinel, element multiplier, or overflow check before writes
pointer write through p+n or p-- where n may be negative or greater than buffer length
Java JNI, sun.misc.Unsafe, ByteBuffer native address, or System.arraycopy into native/fixed buffer with unchecked length
negative_signals: write guarded by 0 <= index && index < capacity on the same buffer
copy length computed as min(source_length, destination_capacity - used - terminator_space)
snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, ...) or strlcpy/strlcat/memcpy_s with checked return/truncation handling
allocation uses checked multiplication/addition and includes space for NUL terminator or sentinel
Java ordinary array store with JVM bounds checks and no native/Unsafe access
false_defense_traps: strncpy can leave the destination unterminated when source length >= destination size
compiler canaries, /GS, FORTIFY_SOURCE, ASLR, PIE, NX are defense-in-depth, not bounds validation
checking source length before expansion or encoding misses output growth such as '&' to '&'
casting negative length or return value to size_t can turn -1 into a huge copy size
checking only upper bound misses underwrite through negative index or pointer decrement
verification_focus: Can any write index, pointer, or copy length reach outside the destination buffer, including off-by-one, negative, and integer-overflow cases?

consequence_chains.trigger: off-by-one boundary or missing terminator space
consequence_chains.consequence: one-byte or sentinel write corrupts adjacent memory

consequence_chains.trigger: allocated buffer size is smaller than the number of bytes or elements written
integer overflow reduces allocation or bounds calculation before copy
untrusted or invalid pointer is used as a write destination

patch_principle: Validate every write offset and length against the destination buffer capacity before writing.
Use bounded APIs such as snprintf, memcpy_s, strlcpy/strlcat, or vetted safe string libraries and check truncation/errors.
Compute allocation sizes with checked arithmetic and include terminators, sentinels, and element-size multipliers.
Reject or truncate inputs before copy and after expansion/encoding size is known.
Enable ASan, FORTIFY_SOURCE, /GS, stack canaries, ASLR, PIE, and NX as defense-in-depth.
